label: Meaning remains
beats: Design decisions should travel with their meaning.
Welcome to Cedar's semantic framework.

label: The cost of repeated decisions
beats: When decisions stay in conversations, teams repeat them.
That translation work slows us down and makes consistency harder.

label: Three connected capabilities
beats: Cedar reduces this friction with three connected capabilities.
A shared semantic framework.
A unified design and development system.
And variables that adapt across platforms.

label: A new semantic layer
beats: The semantic layer sits between primitive values and components.
It captures why a design choice exists, so its meaning survives changes in implementation.

label: The color foundations
beats: Cedar's complete color palettes are our raw material.
O K L C H makes their relationships more perceptually consistent.

label: Color scoped by purpose
beats: The next step is choosing colors by purpose.
Scopes guide what works for text, surfaces, and graphics, reducing guesswork.

label: Start with the user's intent
beats: Begin with the user's intent.
Actions commit or navigate.
Controls configure the interface.
Selections express a choice.
Feedback communicates status.
Universal colors support plain content.
And graphics support visual expression.

label: Five questions in a token name
beats: A token name answers five questions.
The foundation.
The interaction family.
The role.
The identity.
And the expression.
Expression describes how strongly to communicate. It leaves room for future themes.

label: One component, four color roles
beats: One component combines several color roles.
Its surface, border, text, and icon each have a job.
Each can be mapped independently.

label: Action in practice
beats: For an Add to cart button, the intent is Action.
We map its surface and label.
Capture those choices in a component contract.
And generate the styling.
Hover,
focus,
and pressed states express the same purpose.
The user sees one coherent interaction.

label: Control in practice
beats: An accordion is Control.
Map its parts.
See it work.

label: Shared meaning, adaptable expression
beats: Variables let the same semantic purpose adapt to different modes and platforms.
The values can change while the meaning remains.
Shared foundations leave room for native platform conventions.

label: The Semantic Token Migration skill
beats: We're also releasing the Semantic Token Migration skill to make adoption easier.
It guides you through choosing a component.
Mapping intent.
Building a contract.
And comparing the result.
That brings the method into everyday migration work.

label: Less translation, more understanding
beats: Less translation.
More shared understanding.
